quest.title: The Illusion's Finishings
quest.description: In the wilderness of Fontaine, you see a Melusine struggling against some Eremites.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: A Brush of Seafoam and Crimson

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Battle) I don't mind.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Straightforward, huh? Well, that saves us time as well!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: See, what did I tell you...

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (The sound of rummaging comes from beyond the door...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, that was louder than Paimon thought it would be.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Uh... My paints... But they should be here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we've said a lot so far, but what should we call you, again?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Mamere. My name is Mamere. I was painting here, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so Melusines can paint too?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Yes... I do. Every day, in fact. Because painting the things that I want to brings me happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, aren't you a painter, then?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: I see. I'm not sure I understand what you mean, but I guess so.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Anyway, let's help gather up the painting tools first, {NICKNAME}. Considering how short her hands are, Paimon's can't even imagine how she'd hold a brush...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: But your hands are shorter than mine...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: ...Thank you. It would take a long time for me to clean them up.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You help Mamere pick up the scattered painting tools...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, looks like we're more or less done! Good job, Paimon!

choices.text: It was mostly me doing the work...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: You barely did anything, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey, it's called a division of labor!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, what were those people actually trying to do?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Them? Hmm... They wanted to exchange Mora for the paintings in my hands.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so they wanted to— wait, then they were here to buy your art after all, weren't they?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh oh, wh—what do we do? Sounds like we had good intentions, but we ended up interrupting a business transaction you were having...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Business? I... don't think you could call it that. Don't both sides have to exchange things the other needs for it to be called "business"?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I don't need Mora... so that wasn't business.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't need Mora? Wait, you're not some sorta renowned painter, are you?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Renown? Does that mean that people know about you?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I guess I count then? Previously, a stranger claiming to be an art collector or something asked to exchange a large sum of Mora for my artwork...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A self-proclaimed collector came to you!? And they cited a high price, to boot... No wonder you said you didn't need Mora. If Paimon could sell her paintings for that much...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Hmm? Can you draw too, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err, not really. But maybe, with some hard work, starting today...

choices.text: Reckon it's too late for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows, but ooh, this makes her so envious...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, who's that collector you were talking about, anyway?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: A rather cool person. And... quite gentle, too.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: If he hadn't suddenly mentioned Mora, I would have just given him the painting as a gift... Why do these tall people always love talking about that stuff...

choices.text: Yes, you can't put a price on art.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Well, I wouldn't say that, exactly, but it's Mora that I would say has no specific relation to art...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Mamere, could Paimon have a look at your paintings? Paimon's curious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About the value of the art, I presume.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Paimon's not always thinking about that stuff! This is appreciation! Appreciation of art! Nothing else, alright?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Hmm? Sure, but...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: If you're so interested, Paimon, why don't I just draw a portrait for the two of you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Would you really?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: You helped me chase those troublesome people away, and you helped me gather up my painting tools. I've actually been wondering how to thank you all this time.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: It's just... Would a painting be too odd of a thank-you gift to give?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, of course not!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, Mamere. Could we give you some directions regarding the painting, by the way?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Hmm? Sure.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: But before that, I'll need to re-pack my painting tools. Those people knocked my paint buckets over, so there's no way I can work here. I'll need to make a trip home first.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, could you wait for me in the village? I'll clean up over here and head down soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The village?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Hmm? Ah, right. It's our home — we call it "Merusea Village."

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: You just need to swim down from over here and then keep going forward...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay then. Let's go!

choices.text: I don't think this is a matter of height...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course. After all, Mora is— Well, actually, Paimon doesn't think you can evaluate art solely based on Mora either...

choices.text: Not with that attitude you won't.
Good job me, more like!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, they're gone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright? Are you hurt in any way?
I'm fine... But are you really people from that, uh, Maison Lumitoile place? You seem so strong...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, we were just trying to fool them! {NICKNAME} made that one up on the fly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #But that did the trick, didn't it? {NICKNAME} does cut an upright and imposing figure — and Paimon's pretty cool and official-looking, right?

choices.text: An upstanding person — yes, that's me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Standing straighter than your trusty Dull Blade!

choices.text: ...Paimon, cool?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And she'd be twice as cool if she wore the uniform!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They ran off, huh... Why do these people always need to take a beating before they'll cool off, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But never mind that. Are you okay?
...I'm fine. Thank you. I'm... not very good at dealing with such people.
You're... very impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. Well, we are well-honed professional adventurers, after all! People like that can't hold a candle to us, that's for sure!
#No... I don't mean {M#his}{F#her} skills. Anyway, {M#he}{F#she} was the only one fighting. You were just watching...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, Paimon's a guide! We're just splitting the work, y'know. Right, {NICKNAME}?
I didn't expect to meet anyone else here. Are you here to gather inspiration, too?
This is a rather deserted place, but it is very beautiful. A painting that draws its inspiration from this place will surely be beloved.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Mamere!?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Are you surprised, Paimon? And happy, that we have met again after all this while?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it hasn't exactly been a "long while" since we last met... Actually, how did you get back sooner than us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't see you at all, either!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: I came back immediately after packing, and I wound up waiting for you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, alright then. Also, is this Merusea Village? All the houses are kinda small — pretty interesting...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we've got a Melusine Chef, a Melusine Adventurer, or a Melusine Architect who specializes in building Melusine houses in this village! Hey, Mamere, what does your house look like?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: My house is pretty and quiet. It's a good place to paint. Come on, it's this way.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Well. Um, this place is my house. Ahem! And, uh... Welcome to my humble abode. Please don't mind the mess and... all comments are welcome, and...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No need to be so formal! So, this place is a quiet spot suited for painting because it's a good distance from the village, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: I'm back, Seymour.
*garbled mechanical noises* Welcome back, milady. You are as gentle, lovely, and radiant as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Did that robot dog just talk!?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #Yes! Paimon, {NICKNAME}, this is Seymour — he's family!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #Seymour, these two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon. They're nice people who stopped others from giving me Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't phrase it like that! You make it sound like we did something bad...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, never mind that. Why can Seymour speak?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: What do you mean? Of course he can — there'd be something wrong with him if that wasn't the case!

choices.text: Uh huh. What she said, Paimon.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Yup. What I said, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No, no! Stop simply agreeing with people, {NICKNAME}! No robot dog can talk, no matter where they're from!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Hmm... Since you're from abroad, I guess you know what you're talking about. That said, Seymour can talk, and he's also my best friend. He even critiques my paintings.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I see. Your judgment is very sharp, milady.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (It just talked again! Paimon's sure that Mamere isn't doing ventriloquism or anything... But does their exchange really make sense? It feels... mismatched.)

choices.text: Did someone give it to you as a gift?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: That's not it. We met when I was looking for paints nearby once — that's when I discovered poor Seymour lying in a pile of junk, all alone.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: So I talked to him, and we became friends. Later, I brought him back with me so he'd have a home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, does this thing have any other functions other than talking?

choices.text: Seymour, paw.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: #{M#...}{F#I am sorry, milady, but I fear I cannot.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{M#Huh. He seems to only respond to you, Mamere...}{F#...?}

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #{M#Pretty rude, huh, this Seymour?}{F#What's going on?}

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: #{M#...}{F#Apologies. I believe that you know as well as I do, milady.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{M#Well, he's probably just shy! No need to take it personally!}{F#Hmm... He did say some stuff, but he hasn't moved one bit...}

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #{M#Sorry about that. For some reason, Seymour only talks to me.}{F#Ooh, Seymour actually spoke to you! He usually doesn't talk to anyone but me. He must know that you're a nice person!}

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #{M#He falls silent when faced with other people, just like this...}{F#However, he can't move or run around like normal, furry dogs.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True — y'know, he might be one of those clockwork meka! Do you just talk to him all the time, Mamere?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Yes... No one in the village really understands art, so there's never much to talk about. I mean, they care about me — but holding a conversation can be tough.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: They definitely don't show as much interest in my paintings as you do, Paimon! Other than Mr. Jakob, only Seymour ever talks to me about art.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon does wanna see how cool and pretty she'd look in your work. Also, is this "Mr. Jakob" a friend of yours too?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Yup, that's the art collector from before who wanted to exchange my paintings for Mora. He was cool and gentle, and he told me all kinds of things about art. He even said that he could understand those paintings...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (And despite all that, she didn't sell a single one to him in the end, huh...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hmm... The harder something is to come by, the more incredible it tends to be. Wait. Might Mamere's paintings be priceless treasures!?)

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Let's put that aside for now, though. It's time to paint!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh! Is this the moment Paimon's been waiting for? Is a priceless masterpiece about to be created?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I don't think I can do that, exactly... But I will do my best to make a worthy gift for you two all the same!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I'll prepare my tools. Please wait for me, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Let's go look around nearby, shall we?

choices.text: Seymour, turn.
Did you fish this out of the water?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can you really find a "best friend" just like that?

choices.text: Talking robot dogs aren't generally the norm...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Is that so? But Seymour can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Paimon thinks we've seen this type of easel before.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems to be a design from outside the village...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Speaking of that, how do the Melusines of Merusea Village trade with merchants from outside? Paimon doesn't think normal merchants would be any good at diving...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Actually, this could be a great business opportunity for us, don't you think? If we took over all foreign trade for Merusea Village, we'd be rich!

choices.text: Aye, we'd be rich!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? Hehe, that was a pretty good call from Paimon, huh? Let's explore the possibility later!

choices.text: I suspect that wouldn't work...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why wouldn't it work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This box contains...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's rude to go through other people's stuff, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon just happened to see it, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But still... it seems like there's some machine components inside, though they're a bit...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Might these be tools used to maintain Seymour? Guess it might be best not to mess with them, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Paimon's got a question. Why's Seymour the only clockwork mechanism that can talk?

choices.text: It might be some experimental prototype...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. But if that's the case, why did it get left here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You'd think that a new invention from the Fontaine Research Institute would...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waaait a minute... Did the explosive accident at the Institute back then send Seymour flying all the way here?

choices.text: Could it really have been sent flying that far...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... Well, what's the deal with it, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{M#No response... Guess it's just as Mamere said. It only speaks to her.}{F#No reply... Somehow, it doesn't seem all that smart.}

choices.text: Wouldn't Seymour just have shattered on impact?
That's true. What's the deal with you, Seymour?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Yes! I want to draw the most beautiful things.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #Common paints are fine, but they won't be able to portray the warmth that {NICKNAME} emanates or Paimon's shininess.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Give me a second. I'm gonna gather the paints I need.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right. Your hands are so short — it might be tough for you to hold the paint bucket by yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: M—My hands aren't short! Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Also, there's no need to worry. I've always gone out to get paints on my own, so I'm used to it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you don't have friends accompanying you most of the time?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ahem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Uh... What Paimon means is... Um, sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you apologizing?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Oh, I get it, Paimon! You feel bad for me because Seymour can't move and I might be lonely while collecting paint, right? You're so nice... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But anyway, we should go together. It'll be more convenient that way... right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup, let's go together.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Hmm... If you're both willing, then let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Thank you... That makes me so happy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. Well, Paimon really does want to see your work, y'know!

talks.objective: Go to the place to collect the paint

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #Look, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Those are the ores that we need. Now, what we need to do next is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe! Say no more! We're expert miners! We'll show you how the pros do it!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: U—Um, please wait. Digging directly isn't going to work...

talks.objective: Use the prisms to resonate with the ore

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Battle) Looks like there's no reasoning with you.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Hah! You're the one who's disrupting a legitimate business transaction here!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Whatever, this is getting annoying. You two, with me! Let's get this kid!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's how we're doing this, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But as long as we grind this ore into powder, we can make paints, right, Mamere?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Where's Mamere? She was here a moment ago...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She probably went up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously. Someone that small shouldn't go running around like that... Never mind. Let's head up ahead too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Eh? {NICKNAME}? Are you okay? You're zoning out again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing. I'm just a bit dizzy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just like before...? Uh... Have you just not had enough to eat or something?

choices.text: Yeah, thanks, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't push yourself too hard, alright? ...Let's keep going, shall we?

choices.text: Thanks, but I don't think this is a question of how much I have or haven't eaten...

talks.objective: Use the prisms to resonate with the ore again

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we've already gathered loads of stuff. This should do it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Wow! So much ore! I can make lots and lots of paints with these. Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, no need! But they're all red ore... Will you have enough colors to use?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it. Now, time for the last step!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon knows! You're gonna grind the ores and make them into paints! Is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Huh? Hmm. Well, if you put it like that... Counting the need to grind the paints, there should be two more steps instead...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: These ores contain a lot of impurities. If we were to make them into paint like this, the colors won't be even — they'll look dirty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Paimon didn't know that there were so many considerations at play... Guess that's what makes you a master of the arts!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what do we do, Master Mamere?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Hehe. At this time, we need to find purer ores, grind them down, and then mix the powders together.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: This way, the amount of impurities will decrease, and the paints we get from them will be more beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But shouldn't we have just used the purer ores to make the paints from the beginning?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: There aren't that many high-purity ores around, silly! You might as well be saying that "If there's no Tidalga to eat, let's have Poissonchant Pie instead!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that metaphor sure gives you a distinct taste of Melusine food culture... That said, there aren't any other mineral veins nearby, are there?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Yes... We'll need to go further inside this place to find the purer ore we need.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Do you want to take a break? I can take care of the rest. I won't be long anyway!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll go with you... Wait. Look over there! Is that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A red... whirlpool? Wormhole? What is that?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: It's a shortcut. Haven't you seen one before? There should've been many of them along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A shortcut? It looks pretty ominous for one... Is this what they call "a shortcut that's the longest way around"?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Well, I always take paths like these. They're safe. And warm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, uh, if you say so then! We've come this far, so we might as well go all the way in helping you find high-purity ores!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's enough. This is Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: E—Exactly! You know what happens to those who break the law here in Fontaine, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Don't take that tone with me! "What happens to those who break the law," my foot! Who do you think you are, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: I'll say this one more time — stay out of this. This is between us and the kid!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Paimon feels nauseous. This shortcut really was something. Was that... part of Melusine culture too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: On closer inspection, it seems like we did pass this place by when we came down. To think that there was such a large stone over there...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: That's right, and this place feels warm and safe, doesn't it? Father told me about it, and it contains high-purity ores. I'll take care of the ones here, so just wait for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, these don't look all that different from the ordinary sort...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Huh? But their colors are totally different...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: R—Really? Aren't they all red anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Well, yes, but there are pretty obvious differences between different shades of red, right?

choices.text: Huh. I couldn't tell...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I—It's fine. The differences are actually really small. It's normal that you're not able to tell the difference...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, didn't you say they were obvious?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, you probably know a lot more about painting than we do, Mamere, and about ores and paints, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Either way, Paimon didn't know that painting was such tough work! Mining, gathering different ores to make paints... Paimon used to think that it was just about putting paint on canvas...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh? Are you feeling all right, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I hear something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What did you hear? Are you okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't you worry about me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And that's exactly how you get Paimon worried...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could this have something to do with the red ores? Some ores do contain toxins that can affect people's minds...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Mamere's been working with these ores all this time, so they should be fine. By the way, what are they, exactly? Paimon wonders if they'd fetch a good price...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe if we collect some extra and sell it to merchants outside, we might be able to...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ores that are even higher in purity...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon gets it! You mean to say that "the high-purity ores needed for Mamere's paintings as paints are the truly invaluable treasures instead," right? In that case, let's help gather those ores! Hehe, Paimon's looking forward to this!

choices.text: (What was that sound...?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: Huh, it's got such a rich texture — that's certainly different!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Hmm? You're really sensitive to colors... Would you like to paint someday? We can paint together. We'll put your paintings and mine together around the house!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You couldn't tell the difference at all, could you?

talks.objective: Adjust the position of the prism to let it resonate with the ore
Adjust the position of the prism to let it resonate with the ore

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you need to collect the paints yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, sorry for the wait!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Eh? That's...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, we weren't just watching, y'know! We've also collected loads of "pure ore." Awesome, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Alright! Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice! Beautiful paints, here we come! Let's head back, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seem rather pleased, Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Eh? Is it that obvious...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your tail's practically wagging...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: No it isn't!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: But you're right, I am very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can make lots of paint now.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Well, yes, that is part of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? What about the other reasons, then?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Well, let's just head back first!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Paimon's talking to you, y'know!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ugh... Whatever. We'll need to get back to get that painting anyway, so let's just do that, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Me? You can call me Jakob. I am a... traveling collector of art.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Good to see you again as well, Ms. Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Mr. Jakob...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: So... Were all the things you told me lies?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: That "you've never seen paintings like these before," that "you'd like to collect them"... That you could... understand them...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: You did all that... for things that have nothing to do with the paintings themselves, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: You misunderstand, Ms. Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I have never intended to deceive you. Even now, I have nothing but admiration for your work.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: But you called them... "shambolic doodles"...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: And I apologize for my imprecise use of words. I was truly mesmerized by their unpredictable, chaotic nature, and I can appreciate the beauty in them, so incomprehensible to the rest of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Eh? R—Really?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Of course I mean it. Your skills are most "enchanting," and your use of colors and persistence in making your own paints truly make me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't be taken in by him so easily!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Uh... Wait, so this is a trick too...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you want the paints for?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: #...What an interesting question. A fine question indeed, {M#Sir}{F#Miss}.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Let me ask you this instead: what else do you think these paints can be used for?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph. Paimon doesn't know what you wanna do with them, but you can't be up to anything good!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You tried to buy her paintings for a high price, and you also hired people to trouble her and ransack her house... You didn't have to go this far for your own drawings, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Yes, why indeed? Consider that a question for further exploration after this discussion. For now, let me venture a guess: You have just collected the raw materials for the paints, am I correct?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: #In that case, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}, allow me to ask you a question — could you give those materials to me?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I have no quarrel with you. As such, we need not be enemies.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: In return, I can give you any amount of Mora — as long as it is within reason, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why are you asking me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! These paints aren't ours! You should be asking Mamere, shouldn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Are you really hoping for an answer? Or are you simply probing about my attitude?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Regardless, I will answer honestly — you and I both know that Ms. Mamere will{RUBY#[S]cannot} not stop me from obtaining her paints, but that the same cannot be said for you.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: I... I never said anything like that! I'm not listening to you, you liar!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Hush now. Say no more, Ms. Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: #You will give me the correct answer, won't you, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course we will — and that's a big fat "no"! Mamere put in so much effort to create something so beautiful, and yet you're treating her like... like this!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: This is the answer the three of you have agreed on? Well then. Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: First, allow me to thank you for helping me collect these paints.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: And well, though it disappoints me to say this, that will be all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "That will be all"? First you ransack someone's house, and then you say all that stuff — and now you wanna run off?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: You misunderstand. I said "that will be all," not "goodbye."

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Ms. Irus, I'd like to change the original terms of our commission.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Get rid of these people. As for your pay... Will seven times the original amount do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Heh! You don't think you can take {NICKNAME} out with just these few people, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: Y—Y'know, boss, she's right. We won't be able to take that person out by ourselves...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: You're mercenaries, aren't you? You should know more about combat than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Since you have the numbers, why are you fixated on your strongest foe? Is there not someone there who cannot fight?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: You mean you want us to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you think you're doing?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Taking sensible, necessary action toward achieving a future far beyond our imaginations.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Tsk, seven-fold pay... There's no arguing, then. Sorry, buddy!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Eek!?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Please do not mind my appearance, milady. My prime directive is to... *garbled mechanical noises* protect you.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: What...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Sey... mour?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. I am here, milady. You are as gentle, lovely, and radiant as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Please step back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem. We heard it, too! But we don't know anything about clockwork meka, so... What should we do, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Right, so, we'll need some "components."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure, but what kind?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: ...This is what I'm talking about. Pretty, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is... a scrap mechanical part?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Are they really scrap, though? They're so shiny and pretty, and they're everywhere here. Everyone in the village really likes them, and so they all have some...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: When we help each other out, we give the other components as tokens of gratitude. And Xana likes them more than most, so she often exchanges a lot of nice things for them. Oh, but she doesn't seem to be in the village...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So they're currency specific to Merusea Village?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Currency? Oh. I get it. Like Mora! Well, I guess you can say that. Hmm... Even if Jakob were to give me a lot of components in exchange for my paintings, I wouldn't accept... unless it would help me fix Seymour...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, sure. We just need to collect components, right? We'll help!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: No way! They're like Mora, you know. Getting parts for me would be like me asking you to, um... earn Mora for me? That sounds like something a villain would do!

choices.text: It's fine. I'm used to it.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: ...O—Okay. Thank you. You're nice people.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I'll also go hunt them down myself. I really can't ask you to find them for me while I just sit around doing nothing!

choices.text: But we can fix Seymour up faster this way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm. It seems that I must now reveal my true identity...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Identity? What identity?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm an enforcer of the law.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah, that's right! You've got a good eye, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: W—Wait, Sis, what do we do...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: #Wh—What are you worried about? If {M#he's}{F#she's} a law enforcer, I'm the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya! You're just gonna believe everything people say, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: And just look at them! Do they look like folks from the, uh, Mai... Mais...

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: ...The Maison Gardiennage.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: That's right, that's the one. Seriously, what's with the ridiculous name? They're just law enforcement, so they might as well call themselves that!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Anyway, you think we've never seen people from the Maison before? You aren't even in uniform — daring impostors, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: Hey, Sis, she isn't talking...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Hmph! Whatever. Not that there's anything more to talk about, anyway. Let's just take the stuff and go!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: C—C'mon, little one, no need to make that face.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: *sigh* Why did we take this job again? Whatever...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Hey, Kaykubad! What are you doing just watching over there? Just toss her the boss's Mora — then let's take the paintings and go!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: Eh, do we have to, though? He doesn't know what we're doing this far out. Why don't we just take the Mora and...

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: How do they put it again? Favors are more important to deals than Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you guys doing?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Wha... Where did you pop out from?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like you're bothering this young lady.

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: Her? Bothered? We're just here to buy some artwork, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Buying? How much were you gonna pay for one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you don't have any hard figures at all!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Well, that's not our fault — this Melusine won't talk!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if she doesn't wanna talk to you, then she doesn't wanna sell! You're just here to take her stuff, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Take!? This is a fair exchange, a fair and square exchange! We're not gonna short-change her... And what's this to you, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nonsense! Paimon heard that guy over there talking about taking the Mora—

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Tch! Told you to watch your mouth, you...!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: Does it really matter? Haven't we always solved things this way up till now?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Can't you ever shut up? We don't have the time to involve unrelated people! Besides—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you looking at?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Nothing! Buzz off, you're butting into legitimate business here!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: If not, I'm afraid we might have to resort to less... savory methods to settle this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What's this small bottle for?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Only one way to find out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. This looks like... paint? There's only a little left, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}? ... {NICKNAME}? Are you okay?

choices.text: I'm just a little dizzy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we sit down and take a break here first? You might be tired from all that swimming...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm fine now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's good... But don't push yourself, alright? If you feel sick later, just say so!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #Um... {NICKNAME}, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Mamere. Are your painting tools ready?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Um, uh... Again, welcome to my humble abode. Please don't mind the mess and... all comments are welcome...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: But, um... I think... I'm out of paints...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I mean the stuff that should've been in that bottle... a warm and beautiful color...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Anyway, sorry, but please wait here a moment. I'll go to gather some paints — I'll be right back...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No need to apologize! A priceless masterpiece like the one you'll make should also need priceless paints, after all!

choices.text: Huh. A flying white fish...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What? A white fish? Are you sure you're okay?

dialogues.text: Alain's little invention... Might as well have been yesterday since I last saw it.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Huh? ... Boss?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: We searched her place, but we couldn't find the paints you wanted...
You couldn't?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: Y—Yes. We did find some bottles that once contained paints, though. They gave off a very pungent smell that made us feel all queasy...
I see, so the paints have been used up. Well, that's an unfortunate coincidence.
Well then, Ms. Irus, please take your people and clean this place up — as things stand, this would make for too shocking a sight, I think.
As for the "paints"... I'll figure something out later.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Understood...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Um... Sorry, sir. We couldn't complete your commission. Before you could personally come to that little squirt's aid, those two strangers came and stole the moment...
It's fine. I'm not bothered by this.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Well, it's not so much about that... But don't you think that this would count as a case of force majeure, as such? So, um, about the remuneration we discussed previously...
Don't worry. You will be paid as per usual.

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: R—Really? Thank you, sir! Ah, if only all our employers were as good-hearted as you!
Whatever the case, I shan't take up any more of your time — just clean these shambolic doodles up.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Shambolic... doodles...?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Ah.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aaand what are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, purple guy! Are you in cahoots with those thieves who wanted to steal Mamere's paintings? ... Oh, Paimon knows what you're up to, alright!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You hired these people to steal Mamere's artwork to create an opportunity for you to rescue her, win her trust, and then achieve some unspeakable aims...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, not that Paimon thinks getting paints counts as anything unspeakable, but...
#Eavesdropping is a bad habit, {M#good sir, good lady}{F#good ladies}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And you're one to talk! Coming here on the sly and ransacking someone's house when they're not in — you've got some cheek to call others out!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Ugh, wh—what is this...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Outdated junk, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Alain's "own little invention." You've been slumbering for years, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Still wanna go at it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, just stop plotting all this bad stuff! Why are you so obsessed with these paints, anyway? Are they really worth you resorting to such despicable actions...?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Please. I've already told you why "we" are doing this.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: As for you, Ms. Mamere, if we should meet again... I look forward to your future drawings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: #Well then, I'll take my leave, {M#good sir and ladies}{F#good ladies}. Ah yes, and you, thinking machine. Let's go, Ms. Irus. We have other things to do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there, Purple Guy!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: P—Please wait, you two! There's... There's something wrong with Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: *garbled mechanical noises*

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My apologies, Ma...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: S—Seymour!?

choices.text: He might be out of energy...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Out of energy... So you mean...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: O—Oh no... This can't be...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Mamere... Are you alright?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Oh, Seymour... Mr. Jakob... He always intended to trick me by saying all those things like "I love your paintings," "I can understand your paintings"...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: And even worse... He damaged you this badly... I won't forgive him... I won't! *sobs*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mamere, let's go look for an engineer in the Court of Fontaine. They should be able to fix or even improve upon him, and we can also help you find more paints along the way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But let's pack things up a bit first. Oh, Paimon hopes your paintings weren't damaged during the fight.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #Thank you... {NICKNAME} — and you too, Paimon.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: It's just... What's the point of all my old work? If Seymour can't be cured... If Seymour can't appraise these works like he used to...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Artworks that no one understands... Those aren't really artworks, are they? They're just what that person called them — "shambolic doodles."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't say that! Even that Purple Guy said that there was something magical and "inscrutably disordered" about your work. Paimon loves your stuff too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, Paimon's wanted to ask about this since before. What do you mean by everyone in the village "not understanding art"?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Exactly that. No one understands the paintings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bah! They only don't get it because they don't have your artistic background, so they can't get the... uh... hidden meanings! Well, everything's about context anyway, right? That means you'll need societal knowledge and an understanding of history...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhm... What Paimon wants to say is... Can we see the paintings?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You pick a painting up from the ground...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, this is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Paimon doesn't really understand its contents either, but it looks really awesome... and this might sound unsuitable, but it looks like it might be super valuable right off the bat...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's... so beautiful! For example... Uh, these details here, they've really got that... immersive feeling. D—Don't you think so too? The other Melusines probably don't understand it because...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: You don't have to force yourself to say something nice, Paimon. I can see right through you.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Still, I know you're doing this out of the goodness of your heart, so, thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, sorry... Paimon couldn't tell what you'd painted, but... it really is very beautiful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's help pack this stuff up...

choices.text: I can understand it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You mean the content of the painting?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: You don't need to comfort me with white lies. I'll pull myself together, don't worry.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This painting depicts...

choices.text: ...Two bears clapping their hands together.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh! Now that you mention it...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Wait, you... really got it?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: And, um, what did you think of this painting?

choices.text: It's very beautiful.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Really? You don't have to lie, you know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, Mamere, have more confidence! Paimon didn't get your painting, but she certainly thought it was very pretty!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Yes. Yes! Thank you! There are so many things I want to express through my paintings. So many beautiful things I want them to see. It makes me so happy to hear you say that.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Still, this really is the first time someone has understood my paintings. The other villagers think they're very beautiful, but that's all they can tell me...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Then, slowly, I began to understand. Even though they don't get my paintings, they were still trying to be nice to me by saying they look "beautiful." It's really kind of them, but I don't think that's good.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: So I was really happy when Mr. Jakob... Jakob said that he understood what I was trying to convey through my paintings. I thought, "Finally! Someone can see what I want to show."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, that Purple Guy! He's just awful!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Right. But none of that matters now.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Father told me of many beautiful sights. I feel that the world is a lovely place, and it makes me happy. However, I'm not a good speaker, so I want to make others happy through my paintings.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: But most Melusines only know how to encourage me by saying that my paintings are beautiful. I like them too, but I still want to have someone around who gets my paintings.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: That's why Seymour is such an important friend to me. Unlike the others, he pays attention to my paintings and critiques them. That's also why I was so happy when I met Jakob.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: After I first heard what Jakob had said, I thought to myself, "In the future, I should only show my paintings to Seymour. Others don't understand my work, so they only try not to hurt my feelings."

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #But, since you and {NICKNAME} can understand them, that means they're not entirely beyond comprehension! It means that there are people who can really see the beautiful things that I wanted to show!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: So, like Seymour, you're now my best friends, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, uh, Paimon *is* happy about that, but it does feel weird to be compared to a robot dog...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Regardless, let's continue cleaning up, shall we? Ugh, seriously, those bad guys really made a mess of this place, huh...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You help Mamere pick the scattered paintings up...

choices.text: It's worth savoring.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Yes. Yes! You really do get it! There are so many things I want to express via my paintings, and I want to make the audience feel something new each time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Paimon was right, then! They are priceless masterpieces!

choices.text: ...A drowned throne.
...A burning snowfield.
So that's how it was. I see.
(Did he take damage during the battle?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I do recall us helping Albedo gather Starsilver back then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true... But the ore that we picked up then didn't really get put to any use, did they?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Thank you. Sorry, I made you clean up after me again. Y'know, just like when we met for the first time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's fine. We're friends, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Yup!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like you're in a good mood again. That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Yeah. I feel so happy when I'm with you guys, just like how I feel when I'm on a roll with my paintings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, looking at how you're packing things up, Paimon can't help but think that you Melusines really have short hands...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Hmph! Your hands are even shorter, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way! Short-Hands Mamere!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Yes they are! Baby-Hands Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright! Paimon takes it back. But, really, don't those hands make painting inconvenient? Your canvas does sit on a high stand...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: It's alright, since my hands aren't short at all! But... speaking of painting, I really am sorry that I won't be able to paint for you at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: I just... can't leave Seymour like this. I must fix him first — he is my best friend, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Sorry, Paimon. But I'll paint for you once Seymour's all fixed up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Let's go to the Court of Fontaine together and seek out a reliable engineer to help us!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: An engineer...? No, that's not it... I want to fix Seymour myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait. You know how to fix clockwork meka, too?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Strange that you would even ask, Paimon. Of course not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, how are you gonna fix him, then?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Father said that he's seen a lot of machines, both intact and dismantled, so he can teach me how to fix Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Father?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... You've mentioned this "Father" a few times previously. What's he like? A master Melusine engineer with a long mustache? A Melusine with a wrench?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? U—Uh, did Paimon say something bad? Why'd you stop talking...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Yes. Yes. I see...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Here we go again...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait a moment. Who are you talking to?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Are... the ones I have at home not enough? Then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Mamere—! Hello?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yes. I'll try. Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #So... {NICKNAME}, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Wait, you're talking to us again!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Father has told me how to cure Seymour. We just need to collect enough components, and...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Come on, don't worry! I'll paint for you once Seymour is all fixed up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No! We're not worried about the painting! Ugh... Who were you talking to just now?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Father, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And who's that?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Um... Uh, Father is Father? Wait... Can the two of you not hear Father's voice?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The voice, you say... Oh, yeah, of course we did!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh... Has Seymour's breakdown hit her too hard or something? Anyway, let's just go along with this for now! We can comfort her later...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I believe we've met before, yes?
#Commendable memory you have, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}. Yes, we did have the honor of meeting near a cliff before you made a mess of my plans.
It's just that, at the time, I didn't think that you would make the same choice as me and help Ms. Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't lump what we did in with your little one-man-show!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmph. I'll have you know that this *is* the uniform of the Maison Lumitoile!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Maison... Lumitoile...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Hang on a second, what in the world is that!? Who even calls themselves that?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft. To think that outlanders these days no longer recognize the uniform of the Maison Lumitoile...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Wh—What? But what kind of ridiculous name is that? Is this some out-of-season joke?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: Irus, I'd be careful... If nothing else, this person's confidence is not faked.

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: Besides, think about it — do you really think someone who was trying to trick us would use such an obviously nonsensical name?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: You say that, but even so, I doubt anyone would name their department that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Why would anyone— Uh, how dare you call our name nonsensical? Paimon's not gonna take this lying down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Officer {NICKNAME}, inform these ignorant outlanders of our organization's glorious history!

choices.text: There was once a hero who defended Fontaine from the darkness...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Who chose to protect everyone regardless of the means used... Hang on a minute, does Paimon know this person too?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Anyway, that mighty, invincible hero was like a Lumitoile illuminating the night, showing others the way forward!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And that is why we call ourselves the Maison Lumitoile in his honor!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, hmph! How dare you call our name weird!?

response.speaker: Kaykaus
response.text: Uh, um, sorry...

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Hey! What are you apologizing for?

response.speaker: Kaykaus
response.text: #Well, boss, if you look a little closer, {M#his cape and her clothes}{F#their clothes} not only match, but are actually very unique...

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Aren't... they just the same color? Do you think some clothes and some words are enough for people to pose as officials?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. Of course not!

choices.text: In those days, terrible monsters plagued Fontaine's seas...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Wait, like the chi?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Anyway, our founder did battle against those monsters and, like a Lumitoile, lit the seas up once more!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And that is why we call ourselves the Maison Lumitoile in his honor!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Take this new-model Gardemek, for instance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Hey! What in the world's a Gardemek, huh?)

choices.text: This is the product of our latest research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Wait a minute! This story is getting crazier by the second!)

response.speaker: Kaykubad
response.text: I see. I get it now...

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Wh—What do you mean you "get it"?

response.speaker: Kaykubad
response.text: I've heard it said in the taverns that someone saw meka that are more like humans... This could be the equipment this Maison Lumitoile member is using.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Eh? S—So there were such rumors?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *cough* That is correct. Paimon's prime directives are to serve the public, protect the citizenry, and uphold the law...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: According to... the Pumpkin Protocol, those who take advantage of others must not be let off lightly...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: P-Type Gardemek. Load and charge your kinetic cannon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Beep... beep.. boop... Charging complete. Target locked. Um... Jellenergy Cannon activating...

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: W—Wait! What in the world is that? What are you doing?

choices.text: Leave now, and I will revoke my order.

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Okay, okay, we got it, we got it! We'll just leave, alright? No need to do anything crazy!

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Bah! Just our luck — this wasn't in the task briefing, that's for sure!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The Eremites leave in a hurry...

choices.text: Pay the fine first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Uh, no... Whirr... Whirr... Reloading language modules...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Anyway, if you pay the fine and leave this place, we won't look any further into this case!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Or else...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Recharging... Recharging... Activating Lethal Mode...

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Okay! Okay! We just need to pay up, right?

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: U—Uh, We didn't bring any Mora with us, though. We'll need to go back to our camp and get some first...

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Hey, you two, did you hear that? We're heading back to camp to get that Mora!

response.speaker: Kaykaus
response.text: W—Wait, are you seriously...

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Don't ask questions, you idiot! Let's just go first!

response.speaker: Irus
response.text: Heh, these people from Fontaine sure are gullible! Guess we won't have to pay the fine...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The Eremites leave in a hurry...

choices.text: This is a prototype that only we are equipped with.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't you know the face of Fontaine's General Mahamatra?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: Ack! The General Mahamatra!? It's game over for us! Game over!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Calm down, you bone-headed numbskull! Why would the General Mahamatra be here, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, uh, this is a new post based on Sumeru's system...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (N—No, that's not gonna fly, is it? Why did you have to mention the Mahamatra!?)

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Enough! Enough nonsense! If you're intent on stopping us, then we'll just have to show you what for! You two, with me!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're plainclothes officers...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Plainclothes, you say? What do we look like to you, gullible kids?

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: Well, I'd call this less "not being gullible" and more "knowing what to look out for from experience" — weren't you the one who fell afoul of not one, or two, but several plainclothes police, to the point where you nearly got sent to court?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Sh—Shut up, you—!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: A—Anyway, if you really were plainclothes police, you'd know better than us that you need evidence before you can enforce the law, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, um...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Alright, that's it, cut the crap!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: If you're intent on stopping us, then we'll just have to show you what for! You two, with me!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're enforcers of the Corps of Thirty.

dialogues.speaker: Kaykaus
dialogues.text: Eek! It's the Corps of Thirty!? Why are they here?

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Hey, you idiot, calm yourself! Why *would* they be here, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're the, uh, the Fontaine branch of the Corps!

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Seriously? Who do you think the Corps of Thirty are, anyway? Mints that grow in both Sumeru and Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, they could always be Sweet Flowers instead...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Or Specters...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or the Adventurers' Guild, or Katheryne...

dialogues.speaker: Irus
dialogues.text: Enough! Enough nonsense! If you're intent on stopping us, then we'll just have to show you what for! You two, with me!

dialogues.speaker: Kaykubad
dialogues.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, could you wait for me in the village? I'll need to pack my painting tools before heading down there...
